citationRules: Required citation form: "Documented pattern (Source, tier X): mechanism. Applicability here: [observed/inference]. Expected effect on this site: unknown until measured."
Never transfer another company's metrics to the user's site as a forecast.
Tier C sources: cite mechanism/structure only, never quote a number (numbersQuotable is always false).
A pattern never overrides an evidence gate in SKILL.md — it is context for a decision, not a shortcut around one.
lastVerified:"pending" means a human has not yet opened and confirmed the source; do not silently upgrade its tier or treat it as more certain than that.

sources.title: Demystifying SEO with experiments
sources.mechanism: Split templated pages into control/variant groups (hashed by URL or by market) and compared organic traffic over 1-2 weeks; found some 'best practices' (e.g. unique duplicate board titles) had no measurable effect, and moving to JS-rendered content hurt traffic for about a month.
sources.caveats: Source page returned HTTP 403 during research; a human must open and confirm wording before quoting it.

sources.title: Pinterest SEO experiments (secondary summary)
sources.mechanism: Third-party summary of the Pinterest Engineering post above; used only to corroborate the mechanism, not as an independent numeric source.
sources.caveats: Secondary source; defer to the primary Pinterest post for anything beyond the mechanism.

sources.title: SEO Title Tag Optimization at Etsy
sources.mechanism: A/B tested shorter, reformatted title tags across templated listing/shop pages; shorter titles performed better for Etsy's own catalog.
sources.caveats: Source returned HTTP 403 during research; Etsy-specific finding, not a universal rule about title length.

sources.title: Optimizing meta descriptions, H1s, and title tags: lessons from multivariate SEO testing at Etsy
sources.mechanism: Multivariate testing of meta description, H1, and title tag combinations at template scale.
sources.caveats: Source returned HTTP 403 during research.

sources.title: Experimentation & Measurement for Search Engine Optimization
sources.mechanism: Split-tested SEO changes by market (rather than by URL hash) to measure organic-traffic impact of templated changes.
sources.caveats: Source returned HTTP 403 during research.

sources.title: SEO split-test case studies
sources.mechanism: Index of controlled SEO split tests across many client sites (internal linking, rendering, metadata).
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27: functions mainly as a marketing/resource hub with a handful of case studies (meta description removal, breadcrumb placement), articles, videos, and tools -- not a comprehensive searchable database of all split tests. The individual case studies cited elsewhere in this registry are the real sources; this index is corroborating context only.

sources.title: Server-side rendering internal links
sources.mechanism: Split-tested exposing previously JS-only internal links as server-rendered anchors.
sources.caveats: Result was inconclusive at 95% confidence; SearchPilot itself says there is no universal rule here.

sources.title: SEO split-test lessons: nearby location links
sources.mechanism: Split-tested adding contextual links from ~8,000 regional pages to their 6 nearest-neighbor pages (~12 extra internal links/page on average) on a multi-location site. Result: a 7% uplift in organic traffic for the linked variant pages, framed as link-equity starvation being relieved.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 by direct fetch; SearchPilot's own reported result, tier A experiment.

sources.title: SEO split-test lessons: increasing internal linking
sources.mechanism: Split-tested adding links from level-2 to level-3 category pages (via buttons) on Iceland Groceries' e-commerce site. Result: a 25% uplift in organic traffic across both levels, an estimated +9,200 organic sessions/month; both linking and linked-to pages benefited, attributed to improved crawl paths/IA, not just link volume.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 by direct fetch; SearchPilot's own reported result, tier A experiment.

sources.title: Internal linking split tests (tag index)
sources.mechanism: An index of SearchPilot's internal-linking split-test articles: destination-link display, a categories accordion, breadcrumb placement, and internal-linking strategy expansion.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 by direct fetch -- CORRECTED: this index page does NOT contain a distinct anchor-text-variation test as originally described here; that detail was inaccurate and has been removed. Use searchpilot-nearby-location-links and searchpilot-increasing-internal-linking as the actual anchor-text/link-equity evidence for P08.

sources.title: Crawlable links
sources.mechanism: Official requirements for a crawlable link: an <a> element with a resolvable href; guidance on descriptive anchor text.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27: requires an <a> element with a resolvable href, and recommends descriptive anchor text over generic phrases like 'click here'.

sources.title: Introduction to structured data
sources.mechanism: Explains structured data's role in rich-result eligibility; cites self-reported case data: Rotten Tomatoes (+25% CTR on 100k pages), Food Network (+35% visits after converting 80% of pages), Nestle (+82% CTR on rich-result pages vs non-rich-result pages).
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. These are Google's own cited case numbers -- self-reported by the named companies via Google, not independently audited; treat as tier B self-reported, not causal proof for any other site.

sources.title: Eventbrite case study
sources.mechanism: Eventbrite adopted Event structured data across event pages.
sources.caveats: Eventbrite's own case study notes multiple concurrent SEO projects make attribution difficult — quote that caveat whenever this is cited.

sources.title: Jobrapido case study
sources.mechanism: Jobrapido adopted JobPosting structured data (Google's job-search experience). Self-reported results: +182% organic traffic globally, +395% new registrations from organic search, -35% bounce rate among Google Search visitors.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. Self-reported by Jobrapido via Google; single concurrent change is plausible but not isolated from other site changes -- treat numbers as illustrative of the mechanism's potential, not a forecast.

sources.title: HowTo and FAQ rich result changes
sources.mechanism: Google restricted FAQ rich results to authoritative government/health sites and deprecated HowTo rich results in desktop search, Aug 2023.
sources.caveats: Fetched 2026-10-03: the URL returns only the blog archive listing, not the article body, so the FAQ/HowTo restriction wording could not be confirmed. Open the article in a browser and check it.

sources.title: Topic Clusters: The Next Evolution of SEO
sources.mechanism: A pillar page plus linked cluster pages, bidirectionally linked, organizes topical authority around one URL per subtopic.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27: pillar page + cluster pages linked bidirectionally; 5-step process (choose core topics, validate via keyword research, build pillar, build cluster pages, link strategically).

sources.title: Historical blog SEO/conversion optimization
sources.mechanism: HubSpot found 76% of monthly blog views and 92% of monthly blog leads came from older posts (despite ~200 new posts/month across ~6,000 total). Two-part method: (1) update CTAs on high-traffic/low-conversion posts to match the keywords actually driving traffic, (2) refresh outdated content and republish with a new date to signal freshness. Self-reported results: conversion rate increased on every one of 75 optimized posts (one post +240%), organic views of optimized old posts +106% on average, leads from optimized posts roughly doubled (tripled when combined with republishing).
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. Self-reported by HubSpot; republishing with a new date to 'signal freshness' is a judgment call the skill should NOT recommend doing cosmetically -- only update dateModified when content substantively changes, per this card's existing guardrail.

sources.title: SEO content marketing and business potential scoring
sources.mechanism: Scores topics 0-3 on 'business potential' (3 = the product is an indispensable solution to the topic; 0 = no natural way to mention it) and publishes only 2-3 scored topics.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27: 4-step framework (find topics with traffic potential, score 0-3 business potential, create product-led content matching intent, maintain via quarterly audits); recommends prioritizing topics scored 2 or 3.

sources.title: AI Overviews and click-through rate
sources.mechanism: Observational study of 300,000 keywords (March 2024 vs March 2025) found a 34.5% average CTR reduction for the top organic result on queries where an AI Overview appeared, versus similar queries without one.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. Explicitly framed as correlational by the authors, not causal; the article itself notes a Google executive disputing the interpretation. Use only to set realistic expectations in reporting, never as a forecast of this site's CTR.

sources.title: HubSpot's SEO collapse
sources.mechanism: Analyst reporting on HubSpot's 2024-25 organic traffic decline.
sources.caveats: Fetch returned HTTP 403 on 2026-09-27 (unchanged from original research) -- a human must open and confirm before quoting.

sources.title: HubSpot blog rankings drop analysis
sources.mechanism: Independent analysis attributing much of HubSpot's lost traffic to popular topics unrelated to their core business.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27: the analysis attributes HubSpot's blog traffic decline mainly to pages ranking for popular-but-business-irrelevant queries (e.g. 'shrug emoji', 'famous quotes'), and frames it as Google's core update enforcing people-first/topical-relevance guidelines -- the author states this causally, more assertively than 'inference.' Still a third-party analyst's interpretation of public traffic-estimate tools, not HubSpot's own disclosure -- tier C and numbersQuotable stays false regardless of how assertively the source itself is worded.

sources.title: SEO for web migrations
sources.mechanism: Practitioner checklist for URL migrations: full URL mapping, redirects, before/after crawl comparison.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 that the page exists and describes a 'minimum viable' pre/post-migration validation checklist (URL mapping, redirects, before/after audits), but the actual checklist items live in a linked Google Sheet that was not fetched -- treat the mechanism description here as a paraphrase of the page's framing, not a verified item-by-item checklist.

sources.title: March 2024 core update and spam policies
sources.mechanism: Defines 'scaled content abuse' — templated pages generated at scale without unique value per page — as a policy violation.
sources.caveats: Fetched 2026-10-03: the article defines scaled content abuse as many pages generated primarily to manipulate rankings, typically unoriginal content that adds little value. Matches the mechanism.

sources.title: Top ways to ensure your content performs well in Google's AI experiences
sources.mechanism: Foundational SEO practices (indexability, clear answers, unique detail) are what AI features rely on; no separate ranking system.
sources.caveats: Fetched 2026-10-03: the article body supports "focus on visitors, provide unique satisfying content". The card's "no separate ranking system" wording was not found in the body. Check the article before relying on that line.

sources.title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization
sources.mechanism: Lab benchmark found that adding citations, quotations, and statistics improved a page's visibility within a research-controlled generative-engine benchmark.
sources.caveats: Full PDF fetched 2026-10-03: the paper tests Cite Sources, Quotation Addition and Statistics Addition as GEO methods. Lab benchmark only. The up-to-40% visibility figure is the paper's own claim and must not be quoted.

sources.title: How to improve your local ranking
sources.mechanism: Google's official local-ranking factors are relevance, distance, and prominence (Google's own current wording is 'relevance, distance, and popularity'), all improved by maintaining complete and accurate Business Profile information.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. No influence over 'distance'; never recommend fabricating reviews to influence 'prominence'/'popularity'.

sources.title: Tell Google about localized versions of your page
sources.mechanism: hreflang requirements: reciprocal links, self-reference, x-default.
sources.caveats: Fetched 2026-10-03: the doc requires return links, each version listing itself, and recommends x-default. Matches the mechanism.

sources.title: Skyscraper Technique
sources.mechanism: 3-step method: find content that already attracts backlinks in a niche, build something demonstrably better (longer, more current, better designed/more thorough), then email site owners who linked to the original with the improved version. Self-reported case: Brian Dean's own 'Google's 200 Ranking Factors' post saw +110% site-wide traffic within 14 days, 17 backlinks from 160 outreach emails (~11% success rate), and 2M+ referral visitors long-term.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. Single self-reported case, one practitioner; outreach itself is out of scope for a codebase tool (this skill can only help build the asset, not run outreach). A published critique of this technique exists (Ahrefs) and still has not been read this session.

sources.title: How Zapier quadrupled organic traffic
sources.mechanism: Third-party teardown describing Zapier's app/app-pair integration page structure (one page per integration pair, each with unique setup content).
sources.caveats: Fetch returned HTTP 403 on 2026-09-27 (unchanged from original research) -- a human must open and confirm before citing; the structural description (one page per integration pair) is a reasonable inference from Zapier's public site structure regardless.

sources.title: Wise SEO case study
sources.mechanism: Wise's currency-pair/corridor pages (e.g. /send-money-from-us-to-mexico/, /currency-converter/gbp-to-inr/) each combine a real-time exchange rate, market-specific fee comparisons, localized regulatory info, corridor-specific FAQs, and reviews -- not thin templated pages.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27: the source itself states its traffic/index-size figures (~3.8M keywords, ~537,135 indexed pages) are derived from third-party SEO tools analyzing observable patterns, explicitly NOT Wise's own disclosure. Structure only is citable; numbersQuotable stays false.

sources.title: Vodafone Core Web Vitals case study
sources.mechanism: A/B test (~100K daily clicks/34K daily visits from paid media per arm) where the variant moved a widget's rendering from client-side to server-side plus other SSR/image optimizations. Results: LCP 8.3s->5.7s (31% improvement), +8% total sales, +15% lead-to-visit rate, +11% cart-to-visit rate.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 with more precise figures than originally summarized; Google/web.dev-published, Vodafone's own reported A/B test, tier A.

sources.title: Yahoo! JAPAN News Core Web Vitals case study
sources.mechanism: Fixed CLS on article pages by reserving image space via aspect-ratio boxes (backend-supplied aspect ratio) before the hero image loads. Results: CLS ~0.2 -> near 0, +15.1% page views/session, +13.3% session duration, -1.72pp bounce rate, 98% fewer URLs flagged with poor Core Web Vitals in Search Console.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 with more precise figures than originally summarized; self-reported case study via web.dev.

sources.title: The Economic Times Core Web Vitals case study
sources.mechanism: Site-wide Core Web Vitals overhaul (critical-content prioritization, font-display:swap, Brotli compression, ad placeholders, explicit container dimensions, JS task splitting, deferred third-party scripts) across a site with 45M monthly active users. Results: LCP 4.5s->2.5s, CLS 0.25->0.09, FID 200ms-><50ms, and a 43% reduction in overall bounce rate.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27 with more precise figures than originally summarized; self-reported case study via web.dev.

sources.title: Core Web Vitals business-impact overview
sources.mechanism: Aggregates self-reported Core Web Vitals business outcomes across ~17+ companies (Vodafone +8% sales, iCook +10% ad revenue from -15% CLS, Tokopedia +23% session duration from -55% LCP, Redbus +80-100% mobile conversion, Netzwelt +18% ad revenue, Lazada +16.9% mobile conversion, GYAO +108% CTR, and others). Explicitly frames these as engagement/conversion/business outcomes, noting CWV is 'one of many' ranking signals -- not primarily a ranking-impact claim.
sources.caveats: Confirmed 2026-09-27. Each underlying company's number is self-reported via web.dev, not independently audited.

sources.title: OpenAI crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User)
sources.mechanism: GPTBot: disallowing it means the site's content should not be used to train generative AI foundation models. OAI-SearchBot: sites opted out are not shown in ChatGPT search answers, though they can still appear as navigational links. ChatGPT-User: fetches pages live on a user's direct request; OpenAI states robots.txt rules may not apply to it because the action is user-initiated, not autonomous crawling.
sources.caveats: ChatGPT-User's robots.txt applicability is explicitly hedged by OpenAI itself, not just by this skill -- do not claim blocking it reliably prevents live fetches.

sources.title: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler?
sources.mechanism: ClaudeBot: blocking means the site's future materials should be excluded from Anthropic's AI model training datasets. Claude-User: disabling it 'prevents our system from retrieving your content in response to a user query, which may reduce your site's visibility for user-directed web search' (Anthropic's own hedged wording -- not 'removes'). Claude-SearchBot: disabling it 'prevents our system from indexing your content for search optimization, which may reduce your site's visibility and accuracy in user search results' (also hedged as 'may reduce', not a guaranteed removal).
sources.caveats: Anthropic's own wording for Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot is probabilistic ('may reduce'), not absolute ('removes'/'prevents appearing') -- cite it with that hedge intact.

sources.title: Verifying Googlebot and other Google crawlers
sources.mechanism: Google-Extended does not impact a site's inclusion in Google Search, and is not used as a ranking signal in Google Search -- it only controls use by Gemini/Vertex AI training and grounding. GoogleOther is a generic crawler for internal research/development; Google states its crawling preferences don't affect any specific product.

sources.title: Perplexity crawlers (PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User)
sources.mechanism: PerplexityBot surfaces websites in Perplexity's search results and is described as not used to crawl content for AI foundation models. Perplexity-User fetches pages live on direct user request and the docs state it 'generally ignores robots.txt rules'.
sources.caveats: The page does not explicitly state the consequence of blocking PerplexityBot -- it only documents the bot's purpose and recommends allowing it; the blocking consequence here is a reasonable inference, not a direct quote, hence tier B not A.

sources.title: CCBot
sources.mechanism: CCBot crawls the web to produce and maintain an open, redistributable web-crawl archive. The page gives the exact robots.txt directive to block it (User-agent: CCBot / Disallow: /) but does not itself state whether other parties' AI training continues to use previously-archived Common Crawl data independent of CCBot being blocked going forward.
sources.caveats: The claim that 'many AI labs train on Common Crawl data even if this bot alone is blocked' is general practitioner knowledge about how the Common Crawl archive is redistributed and reused, not a statement commoncrawl.org's own page makes -- cite it as an inference about the archive's reuse, not as something CCBot's docs assert.

sources.title: About Applebot
sources.mechanism: Applebot powers Spotlight, Siri, and Safari search-adjacent features; blocking it affects those discovery surfaces. Applebot-Extended is separate and does not crawl pages itself -- it only governs how already-crawled Applebot data is used for training Apple's generative-AI foundation models; blocking only Applebot-Extended does not affect search discoverability, and pages can still appear in search results.
